name: read-guard-prose
body:
Root of the file-access-prose fix (feature agent-refinement). The read-guard permission deny (requirements.requirement.read-guard) is only half the contract: the four distributed agents whose frontmatter denies read/glob/grep on graph-state paths must also SAY so in prose. Today they say the opposite — each `## File access (strict)` section opens "You may read any file and query the code graph, but you **never modify any file**" — so the agent is invited to read exactly what the guard denies. A spec-review run (session-ses_f64e) retried a denied `read` of a durable layer node file instead of reaching the spec through `apg_query`/`apg_review`, burning the run. This root asserts prose and grant agree: graph state — the durable spec node files and the transient plan/feedback stores — is reached ONLY through the apg tools, never by reading those files directly; ordinary source files behind code FQNs stay readable with `read`. Decomposed into the three atomic children below.

Acceptance (review-checked prose laws — never executed): (a) each of `spec-review.md`, `spec-writer.md`, `plan-writer.md`, `plan-review.md` states in its File-access section that graph state is reached only through the apg tools and that the node/transient files are never read directly; (b) no prose sentence claims read access broader than the frontmatter grant — the blanket "you may read any file" line is gone; (c) `agent-builder.md` requires the same positive rule for every generated agent, in both its permission-shape list and its step-6 verify checklist.
